> Don't you think the existing comment in ASVS 4.0 right before these requirements:
> 
> "V7.1 covers OWASP Top 10 2017:A10. As 2017:A10 and this section are not penetration testable, it's important for: • Developers to ensure full compliance with this section, as if all items were marked as L1 • Penetration testers to validate full compliance of all items in V7.1 via interview, screenshots, or assertion"
> 
> Addresses this point?

@davewichers - No, I don't, unless you are doing white box or gray box pen testing. But ASVS states:
> Level 1 is the only level that is completely penetration testable using humans. All others require access to
documentation, source code, configuration, and the people involved in the development process. However, even if
L1 allows "black box" (no documentation and no source) testing to occur, it is not effective assurance and must
stop

It seems clear from the descriptions for ASVS requirement IDs 7.1.1 and 7.1.2 that you are either going to need access to the source code or access to the log files to verify these. (And probably the source code, since you wouldn't know if you've "fired" all the relevant logging events.) IMO, interviews and screenshots are not going to cut it. And I'm not sure that "assertions" are worth anything, especially given the proclivity for humans making so many assumptions and for not remembering all the details in complex software systems. So by that consideration, these should be L2, not L1. If you want an "out" to justify making these 2 L1, then just flat out state something like "While some of these are not verifiable without access o source code, we believe that some of them are important enough to _always_ be done, and thus are making them L1."

So, for that reason, I think this should be re-opened and addressed.
